10.1002_adfm.76243: The buried interface between the hole‐transport layer and the perovskite absorber is critical for the performance and stability of wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells (PSCs). This work reports two novel self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) hole‐transport materials, MeS‐4PACz (with a flexible alkyl chain linker) and MeS‐ρPACz (with a rigid phenyl ring linker), designed to engineer this key interface. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal that the planar conjugated phenyl linker in MeS‐ρPACz significantly enhances molecular rigidity, thermal stability, packing density, and dipole alignment compared to its alkyl‐chain counterpart. This superior molecular configuration promotes a denser and more ordered SAM, which facilitates the growth of high‐quality perovskite films with larger grains, improved crystallinity, and reduced defect density. Consequently, devices incorporating the MeS‐ρPACz SAM exhibit more efficient hole extraction, suppressed non‐radiative recombination, and optimal energy level alignment. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.30% with negligible hysteresis, outperforming MeS‐4PACz‐based devices (22.38%). More importantly, unencapsulated MeS‐ρPACz‐based PSCs retain over 90% of their initial PCE after 2000 h in a nitrogen atmosphere, demonstrating significantly enhanced operational stability. This study highlights the pivotal role of molecular rigidity and conjugated linkers in SAM design for developing highly efficient and stable wide‐bandgap PSCs.

Notably, the designed SEI displays a gradient layered structure, with a Li-Sn alloy constituting the bottom layer, LiF occupying the middle layer, and a composite layer of LiCl and organic lithium compounds forming the top layer. The formation mechanism is primarily attributed to the differential acceleration effects exerted by the plasma shell's electric field on different plasma ions. The gradient SEI exhibits multifunctionality, featuring not only high Young's modulus (13.9 GPa) and enhanced interfacial structural stability, but also enabling the Li-Sn alloy component within the SEI to facilitate the preferential growth of the (110) crystal plane with a low migration barrier, thereby achieving the uniform deposition of Li without dendrite growth. Consequently, the modified Li anode exhibits a low overpotential and high coulombic efficiency, and the corresponding pouch cell shows improved cycling stability. This research provides a pioneering interfacial modification strategy for the fabrication of high-performance lithium metal anodes.
10.1002_inf2.70198: Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibit dynamic structural transformations during electrochemical doping, critically impacting device performance in applications such as bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing. While operando grazing‐incidence wide‐angle X‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) has emerged as a powerful tool to probe such changes, its temporal resolution remains fundamentally mismatched with the rapid ion dynamics in OMIECs, often obscuring transient microstructural states. Here, we introduce a time‐aligned operando GIWAXS methodology that bridges this gap by extending the electrochemical doping time constant through engineered device geometry. This enables real‐time tracking of structural evolution during abrupt doping conditions. Using poly(2‐(3,3′‐bis(2‐(2‐(2‐methoxyethoxy)ethoxy)ethoxy)‐[2,2′‐bithiophen]‐5‐yl)thieno[3,2‐b]thiophene) polymers with distinct molecular weights, we reveal that the microstructural response under abrupt biasing diverges significantly from that observed under conventional voltage‐sweeping conditions. Notably, abrupt doping induces intercalation pathways and reorientation behaviors not captured in quasi‐equilibrium measurements. Our approach provides direct insight into doping‐pathway‐dependent structural dynamics and offers a generalizable strategy for resolving rapid ion–polymer interactions in functional OMIEC systems. These findings highlight the importance of kinetic control in operando measurements and inform the rational design of mixed‐conducting polymer devices for transient or pulse‐driven applications. image
